title.zh: 卷436 列傳二百二十三 沈桂芬 李鸿藻 翁同龢 孙毓汶
title.en: Volume 436 Biographies 223: Shen Guifen, Li Hongzao, Weng Tonghe, Sun Yuwen
title.raw: 卷436 列傳二百二十三 沈桂芬 李鸿藻 翁同龢 孙毓汶

sentences.zh: 沈桂芬，字經笙，順天宛平人，本籍江蘇吳江。

translations.literal: Shen Guifen, style name Jingsheng, was a native of Wanping in Shuntian; his registered domicile was Wujiang in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Guifen, whose style was Jingsheng, came from Wanping in Shuntian, though his family register was in Wujiang, Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 道光二十七年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of Daoguang he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi degree in 1847, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and was made a reviser.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年，大考一等，擢庶子。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianfeng, in the triennial examination he ranked first class and was promoted to junior tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In 1852 he placed in the top class of the triennial examination and was promoted to junior tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 累遷內閣學士。

translations.literal: He was successively promoted to Grand Secretariat Bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive appointments to Grand Secretariat Bachelor.

sentences.zh: 先後典浙江、廣東鄉試，督陝甘學政，充會試副總裁。

translations.literal: He successively presided over the provincial examinations in Zhejiang and Guangdong, served as educational commissioner of Shaanxi-Gansu, and was appointed associate chief examiner of the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: He later supervised the provincial examinations in Zhejiang and Guangdong, served as educational commissioner for Shaanxi and Gansu, and acted as associate chief examiner of the metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 八年，丁父憂。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he entered mourning for his father.
translations.idiomatic: In 1858 he withdrew to observe mourning for his father.

sentences.zh: 服闋，補原官。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he resumed his former post.
translations.idiomatic: After the mourning period he returned to his former office.

sentences.zh: 晉禮部左侍郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Minister of the Left in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Left Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 同治二年，出署山西巡撫，明年，實授。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tongzhi he was appointed acting Governor of Shanxi; the following year he received substantive appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In 1863 he was named acting governor of Shanxi, and the next year received the substantive post.

sentences.zh: 連上移屯、練兵諸疏，並稱旨。

translations.literal: He repeatedly submitted memorials on land reclamation, military training, and other matters, all of which won imperial approval.
translations.idiomatic: He sent up a series of memorials on land reclamation and troop training, each of which met with the emperor's approval.

sentences.zh: 桂芬以山西民食不敷，自洋藥弛禁，栽種罌粟，糧價踴增。

translations.literal: Guifen observed that the people of Shanxi had insufficient grain supplies; since the prohibition on foreign opium had been relaxed, poppies were cultivated, and grain prices soared.
translations.idiomatic: Guifen found that Shanxi's grain supply could not meet its needs: once the ban on foreign opium was eased, farmers turned to poppies, and grain prices shot up.

sentences.zh: 於是刊發條約，飭屬嚴禁。

translations.literal: Thereupon he issued regulations and ordered subordinates to enforce a strict ban.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon published regulations and ordered his subordinates to enforce a strict prohibition.

sentences.zh: 疏陳現辦情形，上韙之，頒行各省，著為令。

translations.literal: In a memorial he set out how matters were presently being handled; the emperor approved it, ordered it circulated to all provinces, and made it a standing regulation.
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he described the measures then in force; the emperor approved, had it circulated to every province, and made it standing policy.

sentences.zh: 旋丁母憂。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he entered mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he entered mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 六年，起禮部右侍郎，充經筵講官，命為軍機大臣。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was recalled to serve as Vice Minister of the Right in the Ministry of Rites, appointed lecturer at the Classic Lectures, and named a Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1867 he was recalled as Right Vice Minister of Rites, appointed lecturer at the Classic Lectures, and named a Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 歷戶部、吏部，擢都察院左都御史，兼總理各國事務大臣。

translations.literal: He served in the Ministries of Revenue and Personnel, was promoted to Censor-in-Chief of the Left in the Censorate, and concurrently served as Minister of the Office for the Management of Foreign Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He served in the Ministries of Revenue and Personnel, was promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief, and concurrently headed the Office for the Management of Foreign Affairs.

sentences.zh: 遷兵部尚書，加太子少保。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of War and granted the title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Minister of War and given the title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 光緒元年，以本官協辦大學士。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangxu he served as Associate Grand Secretary while retaining his former rank.
translations.idiomatic: In 1875 he was made Associate Grand Secretary while keeping his existing post.

sentences.zh: 京畿旱，編修何金壽援漢代天災策免三公為言，請責斥樞臣，諭交部議。

translations.literal: A drought struck the capital region; Compiler He Jinshou, citing the Han practice of blaming the Three Excellencies during natural disasters, asked that the Grand Councilors be held accountable and ordered referred to the relevant ministry for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: When drought afflicted the capital region, Compiler He Jinshou invoked the Han precedent of dismissing the Three Excellencies after natural calamities and called for the Grand Councilors to be held to account; the emperor ordered the matter referred to the ministries for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 桂芬坐革職，特旨改為革職留任。

translations.literal: Guifen was punished with dismissal from office, but a special edict commuted this to dismissal with retention.
translations.idiomatic: Guifen was sentenced to dismissal, but a special edict reduced the penalty to dismissal with retention in office.

sentences.zh: 旋復原官，充翰林院掌院學士，晉太子太保。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was restored to his former post, appointed Chancellor of the Hanlin Academy, and promoted to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon restored to his former rank, made Chancellor of the Hanlin Academy, and promoted to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 桂芬遇事持重，自文祥逝後，以諳究外情稱。

translations.literal: Guifen was cautious and steady in handling affairs; after Wen Xiang's death, he was regarded as versed in foreign affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Guifen handled affairs with caution and steadiness; after Wen Xiang died, he was known as the man who understood foreign conditions.

sentences.zh: 日本之滅琉球也，廷論多主戰，桂芬獨言勞師海上，易損國威，力持不可。

translations.literal: When Japan extinguished Ryukyu, court opinion largely favored war; Guifen alone argued that laboring the army at sea would easily damage national prestige and firmly maintained that war should not be undertaken.
translations.idiomatic: When Japan annexed Ryukyu, most at court favored war, but Guifen alone argued that sending troops to sea would squander strength and harm national prestige, and he firmly opposed war.

sentences.zh: 及與俄人議還伊犁，崇厚擅訂約，朝議紛然；

translations.literal: When negotiations with Russia over the return of Ili began, Chonghou had arbitrarily concluded a treaty, and court opinion was sharply divided;
translations.idiomatic: When talks with Russia over returning Ili began, Chonghou had signed a treaty on his own authority, and court debate grew heated;

sentences.zh: 桂芬委曲斡旋，易使往議，改約始定，而言者猶激論不已。

translations.literal: Guifen worked tactfully to mediate, sent an envoy to renegotiate, and the revised treaty was finally settled, yet critics still argued heatedly without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Guifen mediated delicately, sent a new envoy to negotiate, and the revised treaty was finally settled—yet critics still argued without end.

sentences.zh: 桂芬久臥病，六年，卒，年六十有四，贈太子太傅，諡文定。

translations.literal: Guifen had long been bedridden with illness; in the sixth year he died at sixty-four, was posthumously granted Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, and received the posthumous title Wendian.
translations.idiomatic: Guifen had long been ill in bed; in 1880 he died at sixty-four, was posthumously made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, and given the posthumous title Wendian.

sentences.zh: 桂芬躬行謹飭，為軍機大臣十餘年，自奉若寒素，所處極湫隘，而未嘗以清節自矜，人以為難雲。

translations.literal: Guifen conducted himself with strict propriety; as Grand Councilor for more than ten years he lived as if in poverty, dwelling in exceedingly cramped quarters, yet never boasted of his integrity—an achievement people found hard to match.
translations.idiomatic: Guifen was scrupulous in personal conduct; for more than ten years as Grand Councilor he lived like a poor scholar in cramped quarters, yet never flaunted his integrity—something contemporaries found hard to equal.

sentences.zh: 李鴻藻，字蘭孫，直隸高陽人。

translations.literal: Li Hongzao, style name Lansun, was a native of Gaoyang in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzao, style Lansun, was from Gaoyang in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianfeng he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: In 1852 he earned his jinshi degree, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and was appointed reviser.

sentences.zh: 典山西鄉試，督河南學政。

translations.literal: He presided over the provincial examination in Shanxi and served as educational commissioner of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He supervised the Shanxi provincial examination and served as educational commissioner of Henan.

sentences.zh: 十年，上擇儒臣為皇子師，大學士彭蘊章以鴻藻應。

translations.literal: In the tenth year the emperor chose scholarly officials to tutor the princes; Grand Secretary Peng Yunzhang recommended Hongzao.
translations.idiomatic: In 1860 the emperor sought scholar-officials to instruct the princes; Grand Secretary Peng Yunzhang nominated Hongzao.

sentences.zh: 召來京，明年，特詔授大阿哥讀。

translations.literal: He was summoned to the capital; the following year a special edict appointed him tutor to the Eldest Son.
translations.idiomatic: He was called to Beijing, and the next year a special edict made him tutor to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 穆宗登極，皇太后懿旨命直弘德殿。

translations.literal: When the Muzong Emperor acceded, the Empress Dowager's rescript ordered him to serve in the Hall of Manifest Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Tongzhi took the throne, the Empress Dowager's rescript assigned him to the Hall of Manifest Virtue.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，擢侍講。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he was promoted to expositor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1862 he was promoted to expositor.

sentences.zh: 累遷內閣學士。

translations.literal: He was successively promoted to Grand Secretariat Bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: He was successively promoted to Grand Secretariat Bachelor.

sentences.zh: 署戶部左侍郎。

translations.literal: He served as acting Vice Minister of the Left in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He served as acting Left Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 四年，命直軍機。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was ordered to serve on the Grand Council.
translations.idiomatic: In 1865 he was ordered onto the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 五年，授禮部右侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was appointed Vice Minister of the Right in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In 1866 he was appointed Right Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 遭母憂，皇太后懿旨，援雍正、乾隆年大臣孫嘉淦等故事，命鴻藻開缺守孝，百日後仍授讀，兼參機務。

translations.literal: Upon entering mourning for his mother, the Empress Dowager's rescript, citing precedents from the Yongzheng and Qianlong reigns involving ministers such as Sun Jiahan, ordered Hongzao to vacate his post and observe mourning, yet after a hundred days to resume tutoring while also participating in council affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, the Empress Dowager cited Yongzheng- and Qianlong-era precedents such as Sun Jiahan's and ordered Hongzao to leave office for mourning, but after a hundred days to resume as tutor while still serving on the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 並諭：「移孝作忠，勿以守禮固辭。

translations.literal: She also instructed: "Transform filial piety into loyalty; do not obstinately refuse on grounds of ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: She also said: "Turn mourning into loyal service; do not cling to ritual and refuse."

sentences.zh: 」鴻藻懇終制，不允。

translations.literal: " Hongzao earnestly begged to complete the full mourning period, but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: " Hongzao pleaded to observe the full mourning term, but was refused.

sentences.zh: 倭仁等亦代為陳請，仍命恭親王傳諭慰勉。

translations.literal: Woren and others also petitioned on his behalf, yet the emperor still ordered Prince Gong to convey words of consolation and encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: Woren and others petitioned for him as well, but the emperor still had Prince Gong convey words of comfort and urging.

sentences.zh: 鴻藻連疏稱疾，遂得賜告，卒終制始出。

translations.literal: Hongzao repeatedly memorialized claiming illness and thus obtained leave; only when mourning was fully completed did he emerge.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzao sent repeated memorials pleading illness and was granted leave; he did not return until mourning was finished.

sentences.zh: 七年，捻擾畿疆，鴻藻方里居，以各路統兵大員事權不一，疏請特派親王為大將軍，坐鎮京師，以固北路；

translations.literal: In the seventh year the Nian rebels disturbed the capital region; Hongzao was then living in retirement and, observing that commanders of the various armies lacked unified authority, memorialized asking that a prince be specially appointed Grand General to sit at the capital and secure the northern route;
translations.idiomatic: In 1868, as Nian bandits threatened the capital region, Hongzao was at home and, seeing that field commanders lacked unified authority, memorialized that a prince be appointed Grand General to hold Beijing and secure the northern front;

sentences.zh: 左宗棠、李鴻章為參贊大臣，分扎保定、河間東西兩路，各率所部兵勇相機剿辦；

translations.literal: Zuo Zongtang and Li Hongzhang were to serve as assisting grand ministers, stationed respectively on the eastern and western routes at Baoding and Hejian, each leading his own troops to suppress the rebels as circumstances allowed;
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Zongtang and Li Hongzhang were to serve as assisting ministers, one holding Baoding and one Hejian on the eastern and western routes, each leading his troops to pursue the rebels as opportunity allowed;

sentences.zh: 陳國瑞為幫辦軍務，專統一軍為游擊之師；

translations.literal: Chen Guorui was to assist in military affairs and command a separate army as a mobile striking force;
translations.idiomatic: Chen Guorui was to assist in military affairs and command a separate corps as a mobile striking force;

sentences.zh: 直隸總督官文專顧省城，籌備諸軍餉需，以資接濟；

translations.literal: Governor-General Guanwen of Zhili was to focus on the provincial capital and prepare supplies for the armies to sustain them;
translations.idiomatic: Zhili Governor-General Guanwen was to hold the provincial capital and prepare supplies for all forces;

sentences.zh: 丁寶楨駐紮直、東交界，防賊東竄；

translations.literal: Ding Baozhen was to be stationed on the Zhili-Shandong border to block the rebels' escape eastward;
translations.idiomatic: Ding Baozhen was to guard the Zhili-Shandong border against an eastern breakout;

sentences.zh: 李鶴年駐紮直、豫交界，防賊南竄；

translations.literal: Li Henian was to be stationed on the Zhili-Henan border to block the rebels' escape southward;
translations.idiomatic: Li Henian was to guard the Zhili-Henan border against a southern breakout;

sentences.zh: 直、晉交界，由左宗棠等分撥勁旅扼要駐紮；

translations.literal: On the Zhili-Shanxi border, Zuo Zongtang and others were to detach elite troops to hold key positions;
translations.idiomatic: On the Zhili-Shanxi border, Zuo Zongtang and others were to station picked troops at critical points;

sentences.zh: 並請敕下各該大臣和衷商辦，迅奏膚功。

translations.literal: He also asked that all these ministers be ordered to cooperate in good faith and report swift success.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that all these ministers cooperate harmoniously and report victory without delay.

sentences.zh: 奏入，上遂命各路統兵大臣均歸恭親王節制。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor thereupon ordered that all field commanders come under Prince Gong's command.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, the emperor ordered every field commander placed under Prince Gong's authority.

sentences.zh: 旋起禮部左侍郎，仍直弘德殿及軍機如故。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was recalled as Vice Minister of the Left in the Ministry of Rites and continued to serve in the Hall of Manifest Virtue and on the Grand Council as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled as Left Vice Minister of Rites and continued at the Hall of Manifest Virtue and on the Grand Council as before.

sentences.zh: 十年，擢都察院左都御史，加太子少保。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was promoted to Censor-in-Chief of the Left in the Censorate and granted the title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In 1871 he was promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief and given the title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 時有修葺圓明園之旨，朝臣同起力爭。

translations.literal: At that time there was an edict to repair the Old Summer Palace, and court officials rose together in strong opposition.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then went out to restore the Old Summer Palace, and officials across the court protested in unison.

sentences.zh: 鴻藻亦言：「粵、捻初平，回氛方熾，宜培養元氣，以固根本。

translations.literal: Hongzao also said: "The Guangdong and Nian rebellions have only just been pacified, while Muslim unrest still burns; the state should nurture its vital energies to secure its foundations.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzao also said: "The Taiping and Nian campaigns have only just ended and Muslim revolts are still fierce; the court should conserve its strength and secure the foundations.

sentences.zh: 不應虛糜帑糈，為此不急之務。

translations.literal: Treasury grain and funds should not be squandered on so unurgent a task.
translations.idiomatic: It should not waste revenue on so inessential a project.

sentences.zh: 」乃止。

translations.literal: " The project was then halted.
translations.idiomatic: " The work was stopped.

sentences.zh: 十三年，上有疾，命代批答章奏；

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year the emperor fell ill and ordered him to draft replies to memorials on his behalf;
translations.idiomatic: In 1874 the emperor fell ill and ordered him to draft responses to memorials;

sentences.zh: 旋崩，自劾輔導無狀，罷弘德殿行走。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward the emperor died; Hongzao impeached himself for failure in tutoring and was removed from service in the Hall of Manifest Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor soon died; Hongzao accused himself of failing as tutor and was dismissed from the Hall of Manifest Virtue.

sentences.zh: 光緒二年，命兼總理各國事務衙門。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangxu he was ordered to serve concurrently in the Office for the Management of Foreign Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In 1876 he was ordered to serve concurrently in the Office for the Management of Foreign Affairs.

sentences.zh: 尋丁本生母憂，服闋，起故官，以兵部尚書協辦大學士，調吏部。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he entered mourning for his birth mother; when mourning ended he resumed his former post, served as Minister of War and Associate Grand Secretary, and was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He soon mourned his birth mother; after mourning he returned, served as Minister of War and Associate Grand Secretary, and was transferred to Personnel.

sentences.zh: 時崇厚與俄擅定伊犁約，鴻藻堅持不可，爭於廷。

translations.literal: At that time Chonghou had arbitrarily concluded the Ili treaty with Russia; Hongzao firmly opposed it and argued in court.
translations.idiomatic: When Chonghou had signed the Ili treaty with Russia on his own authority, Hongzao firmly opposed it and debated in court.

sentences.zh: 卒治崇厚罪，議改約。

translations.literal: Chonghou was finally punished, and the treaty was renegotiated.
translations.idiomatic: Chonghou was finally punished and a new treaty negotiated.

sentences.zh: 及法越啟釁，言路愈奮發，劾罷樞臣。

translations.literal: When the Franco-Vietnamese conflict erupted, the censorate grew ever more vehement and impeached the Grand Councilors from office.
translations.idiomatic: When war broke out between France and Vietnam, memorialists grew bolder and impeached the Grand Councilors out of office.

sentences.zh: 鴻藻謫遷內閣學士。

translations.literal: Hongzao was demoted to Grand Secretariat Bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzao was demoted to Grand Secretariat Bachelor.

sentences.zh: 後復累遷禮部尚書。

translations.literal: Later he was again successively promoted to Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted again, eventually to Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 十三年，河決鄭州，上命鴻藻馳往督辦。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year the Yellow River burst its banks at Zhengzhou; the emperor ordered Hongzao to hurry there and supervise repairs.
translations.idiomatic: In 1887 the Yellow River broke at Zhengzhou; the emperor ordered Hongzao to rush there and supervise the works.

sentences.zh: 先是河道總督李鶴年、河南巡撫倪文蔚議於西壩興工，鴻藻至，仍之。

translations.literal: Earlier, River Conservancy Director Li Henian and Henan Governor Ni Wenwei had agreed to begin work at the western embankment; when Hongzao arrived, he continued the plan.
translations.idiomatic: River Conservancy Director Li Henian and Henan Governor Ni Wenwei had already planned work on the western embankment; Hongzao upheld their plan on arrival.

sentences.zh: 又續興東壩工。

translations.literal: He also continued work on the eastern embankment.
translations.idiomatic: He also pressed ahead with the eastern embankment project.

sentences.zh: 疊遇奇險，皆力為固守。

translations.literal: Repeatedly encountering extraordinary hazards, he strove to hold every position firm.
translations.idiomatic: Despite repeated crises he did everything to hold the works firm.

sentences.zh: 會伏秋汛至，西壩失事，請暫停工。

translations.literal: When the autumn flood season arrived, the western embankment failed; he requested a temporary halt to construction.
translations.idiomatic: When the autumn floods came, the western embankment gave way, and he asked to suspend work temporarily.

sentences.zh: 上以鴻藻督率無方，革職留任；

translations.literal: The emperor, holding that Hongzao had supervised ineffectively, punished him with dismissal with retention;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor blamed Hongzao for poor supervision and punished him with dismissal while retaining him in office;

sentences.zh: 並奪李鶴年河道總督，命鴻藻暫行署理。

translations.literal: Li Henian was also stripped of the post of River Conservancy Director, and Hongzao was ordered to act in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: Li Henian was removed as River Conservancy Director, and Hongzao was ordered to act in his place.

sentences.zh: 尋回京，復以禮部具奏典禮漏繕簽改日期，再議革職，上特寬免。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he returned to the capital; the Ministry of Rites then submitted a ceremonial document with a misdated endorsement slip, and dismissal was again proposed, but the emperor specially granted leniency.
translations.idiomatic: He soon returned to Beijing; the Ministry of Rites then submitted a ceremonial document with a misdated endorsement, and dismissal was proposed again, but the emperor specially spared him.

sentences.zh: 大婚禮成，復原官。

translations.literal: After the grand wedding ceremonies were completed, he was restored to his former rank.
translations.idiomatic: After the grand wedding he was restored to his former rank.

sentences.zh: 二十年，日韓事棘，命鴻藻商辦軍務，再授軍機大臣。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, as the Korean crisis grew acute, Hongzao was ordered to consult on military affairs and again appointed Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1894, as the Korean crisis sharpened, Hongzao was ordered to advise on military affairs and again made Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 與翁同龢皆主戰，並爭和約，卒不能阻。

translations.literal: He and Weng Tonghe both favored war and together opposed the peace treaty, but in the end could not prevent it.
translations.idiomatic: He and Weng Tonghe both favored war and fought the peace treaty together, but could not stop it in the end.

sentences.zh: 旋以禮部尚書協辦大學士，調吏部。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he served as Minister of Rites and Associate Grand Secretary and was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon Minister of Rites and Associate Grand Secretary, then transferred to Personnel.

sentences.zh: 歷蒙頒賞書畫及諸上方珍物。

translations.literal: He repeatedly received imperial gifts of paintings, calligraphy, and other precious objects from the palace.
translations.idiomatic: He received repeated imperial gifts of paintings, calligraphy, and other treasures from the palace.

sentences.zh: 充鄉試、會試、殿試等閱卷大臣。

translations.literal: He served as chief examiner for the provincial, metropolitan, and palace examinations.
translations.idiomatic: He served as chief examiner for the provincial, metropolitan, and palace examinations.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，以病乞假，疾篤，賞給藥餌，命御醫往視。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he begged leave on grounds of illness; when his illness grew grave, the emperor bestowed medicines and ordered the imperial physician to visit him.
translations.idiomatic: In 1897 he asked for sick leave; when his illness worsened, the emperor sent medicines and ordered the imperial physician to attend him.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十有八。

translations.literal: He died at seventy-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-eight.

sentences.zh: 遺疏入，上震悼，予諡文正，贈太子太傅。

translations.literal: When his final memorial reached the throne, the emperor was deeply shaken with grief, granted the posthumous title Wenzheng, and posthumously made him Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When his death memorial arrived, the emperor was deeply grieved, granted the posthumous title Wenzheng, and posthumously made him Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 子焜瀛、煜瀛，均賞給郎中。

translations.literal: His sons Kunying and Yuying were both granted the rank of director in a ministry.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Kunying and Yuying were both granted the rank of director in a ministry.

sentences.zh: 鴻藻性至孝，為學守程硃，務實踐，持躬儉約。

translations.literal: Hongzao was profoundly filial by nature; in learning he adhered to the Cheng-Zhu school and stressed practical conduct, and he was frugal in personal habits.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzao was deeply filial by nature; in scholarship he followed the Cheng-Zhu school and valued practice over theory, and he lived frugally.

sentences.zh: 傅穆宗十餘年，盡心啟沃。

translations.literal: He tutored the Muzong Emperor for more than ten years and devoted himself wholeheartedly to nurturing him.
translations.idiomatic: He instructed Emperor Tongzhi for more than ten years and devoted himself wholeheartedly to the young emperor's development.

sentences.zh: 一日，穆宗學書，故為戲筆。

translations.literal: One day the Muzong Emperor was practicing calligraphy and deliberately made playful, careless strokes.
translations.idiomatic: One day, while the emperor was practicing calligraphy, he deliberately scrawled in play.

sentences.zh: 鴻藻立前捧上手曰：「皇上心不靜，請少息。

translations.literal: Hongzao stepped forward, took the emperor's hand, and said: "Your Majesty's mind is not calm; please rest a moment.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzao stepped forward, took the emperor's hand, and said: "Your Majesty's mind is unsettled; please pause a moment.

sentences.zh: 」穆宗改容謝之。

translations.literal: " The Muzong Emperor changed his expression and apologized.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor immediately composed himself and apologized.

sentences.zh: 其在樞府，獨守正持大體。

translations.literal: In the Grand Council he alone upheld the larger principles with integrity.
translations.idiomatic: In the Grand Council he alone held to the larger principles with integrity.

sentences.zh: 御史王鵬運諫止修頤和園，幾獲重譴，鴻藻力解之，得免。

translations.literal: Censor Wang Pengyun memorialized to stop repairs at the Summer Palace and nearly incurred severe punishment; Hongzao strongly interceded for him and he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: When Censor Wang Pengyun protested against restoring the Summer Palace and nearly suffered severe punishment, Hongzao intervened forcefully and saved him.

sentences.zh: 德宗間日一往頤和園侍起居，時留駐蹕。

translations.literal: The Guangxu Emperor went every other day to the Summer Palace to attend the Empress Dowager; he sometimes stayed there for extended periods.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangxu went to the Summer Palace every other day to attend the Empress Dowager, and sometimes stayed there for long stretches.

sentences.zh: 言官有言其不便者，太后大怒，欲黜之，鴻藻謂如此必失天下臣民之望，乃止。

translations.literal: When censors criticized the inconvenience of this, the Empress Dowager was greatly angered and wished to dismiss them; Hongzao said that doing so would surely lose the trust of officials and people throughout the empire, and she desisted.
translations.idiomatic: When censors criticized the arrangement, the Empress Dowager was furious and wished to dismiss them; Hongzao said this would surely forfeit the trust of officials and people everywhere, and she relented.

sentences.zh: 所薦引多端士。

translations.literal: Those he recommended and advanced were mostly men of talent.
translations.idiomatic: Most of those he recommended and advanced were men of talent.

sentences.zh: 朝列有清望者，率倚以為重，然亦不免被劫持雲。

translations.literal: Officials at court with reputation for integrity generally relied on him for support, yet he was not entirely free from being pressured, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Men of standing at court generally leaned on him, yet he was not entirely free from pressure, it is said.

sentences.zh: 翁同龢，字叔平，江蘇常熟人，大學士心存子。

translations.literal: Weng Tonghe, style name Shuping, was a native of Changshu in Jiangsu and son of Grand Secretary Weng Xincun.
translations.idiomatic: Weng Tonghe, style Shuping, was from Changshu in Jiangsu, son of Grand Secretary Weng Xincun.

sentences.zh: 咸豐六年一甲一名進士，授修撰。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Xianfeng he placed first in the jinshi examination with top honors and was appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: In 1856 he took first place in the jinshi examination and was appointed reviser.

sentences.zh: 八年，典試陝甘，旋授陝西學政，乞病回京。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he presided over the Shaanxi-Gansu examination, then was appointed educational commissioner of Shaanxi; he begged leave on grounds of illness and returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In 1858 he supervised the Shaanxi-Gansu examination, was appointed educational commissioner of Shaanxi, then asked for sick leave and returned to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，擢贊善。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he was promoted to tutor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1862 he was promoted to tutor.

sentences.zh: 典山西試。

translations.literal: He presided over the Shanxi provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: He supervised the Shanxi provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 父憂歸，服闋，轉中允。

translations.literal: Upon his father's death he returned home; when mourning ended he was transferred to junior mentor.
translations.idiomatic: He went home for his father's mourning; when it ended he was made junior mentor.

sentences.zh: 命在弘德殿行走，五日一進講，於簾前說治平寶鑑，兩宮皇太后嘉之。

translations.literal: He was ordered to serve in the Hall of Manifest Virtue, lecturing every five days; before the curtain he expounded the Mirror of Good Governance, and both Empress Dowagers praised him.
translations.idiomatic: He was assigned to the Hall of Manifest Virtue, lecturing every five days and expounding the Mirror of Good Governance before the curtain; both Empress Dowagers commended him.

sentences.zh: 累遷內閣學士。

translations.literal: He was successively promoted to Grand Secretariat Bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: He rose successively to Grand Secretariat Bachelor.

sentences.zh: 母憂服闋，起故官。

translations.literal: When mourning for his mother ended, he resumed his former post.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother's mourning he returned to his former office.

sentences.zh: 同龢居講席，每以憂勤惕厲，啟沃聖心。

translations.literal: While serving at the lecture seat, Tonghe always urged vigilance and diligence to nurture the emperor's mind.
translations.idiomatic: At the lecture seat he constantly urged vigilance and diligence to cultivate the emperor's mind.

sentences.zh: 當八年武英殿之災也，恭錄康熙、嘉慶兩次遇災修省聖訓進禦，疏言：「變不虛生，遇災而懼。

translations.literal: When the Hall of Military Glory burned in the eighth year, he respectfully copied the sage instructions of the Kangxi and Jiaqing emperors on self-examination after disasters and presented them to the throne, memorializing: "Calamities do not arise without cause; one must fear them when they come.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hall of Military Glory burned in 1882, he copied the Kangxi and Jiaqing emperors' instructions on self-examination after disasters and presented them, writing: "Calamities do not arise without cause; one must fear them when they strike.

sentences.zh: 宜停不急之工，惜無名之費。

translations.literal: Unurgent works should be halted and nameless expenses spared.
translations.idiomatic: Unurgent projects should stop and pointless spending be cut.

sentences.zh: 開直臣忠諫之路，杜小人幸進之門。

translations.literal: Open the path for loyal remonstrance by upright ministers and close the door to petty men who advance by flattery.
translations.idiomatic: Open the way for upright ministers to speak frankly and shut the door on petty men who advance by flattery.

sentences.zh: 」上覽奏動容。

translations.literal: " When the emperor read the memorial his expression changed.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor read the memorial and was visibly moved.

sentences.zh: 又圓明園方興工，商人李光昭矇報木價，為李鴻章所劾論罪。

translations.literal: At the same time work had begun on the Old Summer Palace; the merchant Li Guangzhao had falsely reported timber prices and was impeached and punished by Li Hongzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile the Old Summer Palace was under repair; merchant Li Guangzhao had falsified timber prices and was impeached and punished on Li Hongzhang's motion.

sentences.zh: 廷臣多執此入諫，恭親王等尤力諍，上不懌。

translations.literal: Many court officials seized on this to remonstrate; Prince Gong and others argued especially forcefully, displeasing the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Many officials used the case to remonstrate; Prince Gong and others argued especially hard, to the emperor's displeasure.

sentences.zh: 同龢面陳江南輿論，中外人心惶惑，請聖意先定，待時興修。

translations.literal: Tonghe stated in person the opinion of the Jiangnan public and that hearts at home and abroad were unsettled, asking that the emperor's mind be settled first and repairs wait for a better time.
translations.idiomatic: Tonghe told the emperor face to face of Jiangnan opinion and widespread anxiety at home and abroad, asking him to settle his mind first and postpone repairs until the time was right.

sentences.zh: 乃議定停園工，並有停工程、罷浮費、求直言之諭。

translations.literal: It was then decided to halt the garden works, and edicts were issued to stop projects, abolish wasteful spending, and seek blunt counsel.
translations.idiomatic: The garden works were halted, with edicts to stop projects, cut waste, and welcome frank speech.

sentences.zh: 光緒元年，署刑部右侍郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangxu he served as acting Vice Minister of the Right in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In 1875 he served as acting Right Vice Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 明年四月，上典學毓慶宮，命授讀，再辭，不允。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the following year the emperor began study in the Palace of Nurturing Joy; he was ordered to tutor him, declined twice, and was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The next April the emperor began study in the Palace of Nurturing Joy; Tonghe was ordered to tutor him, declined twice, and was refused.

sentences.zh: 旋遷戶部，充經筵講官，晉都察院左都御史。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue, appointed lecturer at the Classic Lectures, and promoted to Censor-in-Chief of the Left in the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to Revenue, made lecturer at the Classic Lectures, and promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 遷刑部尚書，調工部。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Justice and then to the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He became Minister of Justice, then was transferred to Works.

sentences.zh: 六年，廷臣爭俄約久不決，懿旨派惇親王、醇親王及同龢與潘祖廕每日在南書房看摺件電報，擬片進呈取進止，至俄約改定始止。

translations.literal: In the sixth year court officials long debated the Russian treaty without resolution; a rescript from the Empress Dowager assigned Prince Dun, Prince Chun, Tonghe, and Pan Zuyin to review memorials and telegrams daily in the Southern Study, draft summaries for imperial decision, continuing until the Russian treaty was revised.
translations.idiomatic: In 1880 the Russian treaty debate dragged on; the Empress Dowager assigned Prince Dun, Prince Chun, Tonghe, and Pan Zuyin to review memorials and telegrams daily in the Southern Study and draft summaries for her decision, until the treaty was revised.

sentences.zh: 八年，命充軍機大臣。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was ordered to serve on the Grand Council.
translations.idiomatic: In 1882 he was ordered onto the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 十年，法越事起，同龢主一面進兵，一面與議，庶有所備。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, when the Franco-Vietnamese conflict erupted, Tonghe favored advancing troops while also negotiating, so that the state would have something to rely on.
translations.idiomatic: In 1884, when war with France over Vietnam began, Tonghe favored advancing troops while also negotiating, so the court would not be caught unprepared.

sentences.zh: 又言劉永福不足恃，非增重兵出關不可。

translations.literal: He also said Liu Yongfu could not be relied upon and that substantial reinforcements must be sent beyond the border.
translations.idiomatic: He also said Liu Yongfu was not dependable and that major reinforcements must cross the border.

sentences.zh: 旋與軍機王大臣同罷，仍直毓慶宮。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was dismissed from the Grand Council along with the other councilors but continued to serve in the Palace of Nurturing Joy.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon dismissed from the Grand Council with the other councilors but remained at the Palace of Nurturing Joy.

sentences.zh: 前後充會試總裁、順天鄉試考官，兩蒙賜「壽」，加太子太保，賜雙眼花翎、紫韁。

translations.literal: He successively served as chief examiner of the metropolitan examination and examiner of the Shuntian provincial examination, twice received the character "longevity" as an imperial gift, was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and granted double-eyed peacock feathers and a purple bridle.
translations.idiomatic: He served as metropolitan chief examiner and Shuntian examiner, twice received the imperial gift of the character "longevity," was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and granted double-eyed peacock feathers and a purple bridle.

sentences.zh: 嘗請假修墓，傳旨海上風險，命馳驛回京，恩眷甚篤。

translations.literal: Once when he begged leave to repair his family's tomb, an edict noted the dangers of travel by sea and ordered him to return to the capital by courier post; imperial favor toward him was very deep.
translations.idiomatic: Once when he asked leave to repair his family's tomb, an edict cited the dangers of sea travel and ordered him back to Beijing by courier; imperial favor ran very deep.

sentences.zh: 二十年，再授軍機大臣。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was again appointed Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1894 he was again made Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 懿旨命撤講，上請如故。

translations.literal: A rescript from the Empress Dowager ordered that lectures be withdrawn; the emperor asked that they continue as before.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager ordered lectures withdrawn; the emperor asked that they continue unchanged.

sentences.zh: 同龢善伺上意，得遇事進言。

translations.literal: Tonghe was skilled at reading the emperor's mind and thus able to speak up when matters arose.
translations.idiomatic: Tonghe was adept at reading the emperor's mood and could speak frankly when occasions arose.

sentences.zh: 上親政久，英爽非復常度，剖決精當。

translations.literal: The emperor had long taken personal rule; his spirit was keen and no longer ordinary, and his decisions were precise.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had ruled in person for years; his mind was sharp and no longer what it had been, and his judgments were exact.

sentences.zh: 每事必問同龢，眷倚尤重。

translations.literal: On every matter he asked Tonghe, and reliance on him was especially heavy.
translations.idiomatic: He consulted Tonghe on every matter, and his trust in him was especially great.

sentences.zh: 時日韓起釁，同龢與李鴻藻主戰，孫毓汶、徐用儀主和。

translations.literal: At that time trouble arose between China, Japan, and Korea; Tonghe and Li Hongzao favored war, while Sun Yuwen and Xu Yongyi favored peace.
translations.idiomatic: As the Korean crisis sharpened, Tonghe and Li Hongzao favored war while Sun Yuwen and Xu Yongyi favored peace.

sentences.zh: 會海陸軍皆敗，懿旨命赴天津傳諭李鴻章詰責之，同龢並言太后意決不即和。

translations.literal: When both land and sea forces were defeated, a rescript ordered him to go to Tianjin and convey the throne's rebuke to Li Hongzhang; Tonghe also said the Empress Dowager's mind was firmly set against immediate peace.
translations.idiomatic: When army and navy both failed, a rescript sent him to Tianjin to rebuke Li Hongzhang; Tonghe also said the Empress Dowager would not accept peace at once.

sentences.zh: 歸薦唐仁廉忠赤可用，請設巡防處籌辦團防。

translations.literal: On returning he recommended Tang Renlian as loyal and usable and asked that a patrol defense office be established to organize local defense.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he recommended Tang Renlian as loyal and capable and asked that a patrol office be set up to organize local defense.

sentences.zh: 於是命恭親王督辦軍務，同龢、鴻藻等會商辦理。

translations.literal: Thereupon Prince Gong was ordered to supervise military affairs, and Tonghe, Hongzao, and others were to consult and handle matters together.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Gong was then ordered to supervise military affairs, with Tonghe, Hongzao, and others to consult together.

sentences.zh: 上嘗問諸臣：「時事至此，和戰皆無可恃！

translations.literal: The emperor once asked the ministers: "Affairs have come to this pass—neither war nor peace can be relied upon!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once asked his ministers: "Matters have come to this—neither war nor peace can be trusted!

sentences.zh: 」言及宗社，聲淚並發。

translations.literal: " Speaking of the altars of state, he wept as he spoke.
translations.idiomatic: " Speaking of the dynasty's altars, he wept as he spoke.

sentences.zh: 及和議起，同龢與鴻藻力爭改約稿，並陳：「寧增賠款，必不可割地。

translations.literal: When peace negotiations began, Tonghe and Hongzao fought hard to revise the draft treaty, stating together: "It is better to increase indemnity than to cede territory.
translations.idiomatic: When peace talks began, Tonghe and Hongzao fought to revise the draft, saying together: "Better to increase indemnity than cede territory.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「台灣去，則人心皆去。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "If Taiwan is lost, all hearts will be lost.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said: "If Taiwan is lost, the people's hearts will go with it.

sentences.zh: 朕何以為天下主？

translations.literal: How can I remain lord of all under Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: How can I remain sovereign of all under Heaven?

sentences.zh: 」毓汶以前敵屢敗對，上責以賞罰不嚴，故至於此。

translations.literal: " Sun Yuwen replied citing repeated defeats; the emperor blamed lax rewards and punishments for bringing matters to this pass.
translations.idiomatic: " Sun Yuwen cited repeated defeats; the emperor blamed lax discipline for bringing matters to this point.

sentences.zh: 諸臣皆引咎。

translations.literal: All the ministers accepted blame.
translations.idiomatic: Every minister accepted blame.

sentences.zh: 上以和約事徘徊不能決，天顏憔悴。

translations.literal: The emperor could not decide on the peace treaty and his countenance grew haggard.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor could not decide on the treaty, and his face grew haggard.

sentences.zh: 同龢以俄、英、德三國謀阻割地，請展期換約，以待轉圜。

translations.literal: Tonghe, noting that Russia, Britain, and Germany were working to block territorial cession, asked to extend the date for exchanging ratifications to await a turn in events.
translations.idiomatic: Tonghe noted that Russia, Britain, and Germany opposed ceding territory and asked to delay exchanging ratifications for a turn in events.

sentences.zh: 與毓汶等執爭，終不可挽，和約遂定。

translations.literal: He argued fiercely with Sun Yuwen and others, but in the end could not prevail, and the peace treaty was settled.
translations.idiomatic: He argued fiercely with Sun Yuwen and others but could not prevail, and the treaty was signed.

sentences.zh: 明年，兼總理各國事務大臣。

translations.literal: The following year he was ordered to serve concurrently as Minister of the Office for the Management of Foreign Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was ordered to serve concurrently in the Office for the Management of Foreign Affairs.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，以戶部尚書協辦大學士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he served as Minister of Revenue and Associate Grand Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In 1897 he was Minister of Revenue and Associate Grand Secretary.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，上初召用主事康有為，議行新政。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year the emperor first summoned and employed the principal clerk Kang Youwei and deliberated on implementing new policies.
translations.idiomatic: In 1898 the emperor first summoned Principal Clerk Kang Youwei and began deliberating new policies.

sentences.zh: 四月，硃諭：「協辦大學士翁同龢近來辦事多不允協，以致眾論不服，屢經有人參奏。

translations.literal: In the fourth month a vermilion rescript read: "Associate Grand Secretary Weng Tonghe has lately handled affairs in many ways that do not accord with the court, so that public opinion is dissatisfied and he has repeatedly been impeached.
translations.idiomatic: In April a vermilion rescript read: "Associate Grand Secretary Weng Tonghe has lately handled affairs in ways that displease the court, drawing repeated impeachment and widespread dissatisfaction.

sentences.zh: 且每於召對時諮詢事件，任意可否，喜怒見於詞色，漸露攬權狂悖情狀，斷難勝樞機之任。

translations.literal: Moreover, whenever he is consulted at imperial audience on affairs, he arbitrarily approves or rejects them, and joy and anger show in his words and expression, gradually revealing a disposition to monopolize power in reckless defiance—clearly unfit for duty at the council.
translations.idiomatic: At audiences he arbitrarily approves or rejects what he is asked, joy and anger plain in his speech, gradually revealing a reckless urge to monopolize power—clearly unfit for the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 本應查明究辦，予以重懲；

translations.literal: He ought to be investigated and severely punished;
translations.idiomatic: He ought to be investigated and severely punished;

sentences.zh: 姑念其在毓慶宮行走有年，不忍遽加嚴譴。

translations.literal: yet considering his years of service in the Palace of Nurturing Joy, the court will not immediately impose harsh censure.
translations.idiomatic: yet considering his years in the Palace of Nurturing Joy, the court will not immediately impose harsh punishment.

sentences.zh: 翁同龢著即開缺回籍，以示保全。

translations.literal: Weng Tonghe is ordered to vacate his post and return home, as a mark of lenient preservation.
translations.idiomatic: Weng Tonghe is ordered to leave office and return home, as an act of lenient preservation.

sentences.zh: 」八月，政變作，太后復訓政。

translations.literal: " In the eighth month the political coup occurred and the Empress Dowager resumed regency.
translations.idiomatic: " In August the coup occurred and the Empress Dowager resumed regency.

sentences.zh: 十月，又奉硃諭：「翁同龢授讀以來，輔導無方，往往巧藉事端，刺探朕意。

translations.literal: In the tenth month another vermilion rescript read: "Since Weng Tonghe received appointment as tutor, his guidance has been ineffectual; he has often cleverly used incidents to probe the emperor's mind.
translations.idiomatic: In October another vermilion rescript read: "Since Weng Tonghe became tutor, his guidance has failed; he has often used incidents to probe the emperor's intentions.

sentences.zh: 至甲午年中東之役，信口侈陳，任意慫恿。

translations.literal: At the Sino-Japanese war in the jiawu year he spoke rashly and recklessly urged action.
translations.idiomatic: During the Sino-Japanese War of 1894–95 he spoke rashly and recklessly urged war.

sentences.zh: 辦理諸務，種種乖謬，以致不可收拾。

translations.literal: In handling various affairs he was repeatedly at fault, so that matters became impossible to control.
translations.idiomatic: In handling affairs he erred repeatedly until matters spun out of control.

sentences.zh: 今春力陳變法，濫保非人，罪無可逭。

translations.literal: This spring he strongly urged reform and recklessly recommended unworthy men—offenses that cannot be excused.
translations.idiomatic: This spring he strongly urged reform and recklessly recommended unworthy men—offenses that cannot be pardoned.

sentences.zh: 事後追維，深堪痛恨！

translations.literal: Looking back afterward, it is deeply to be regretted!
translations.idiomatic: Looking back, the harm is deeply to be regretted!

sentences.zh: 前令其開缺回籍，實不足以蔽辜，翁同龢著革職，永不敘用，交地方官嚴加管束。

translations.literal: Earlier he was ordered to leave office and return home, which is not enough to cover his guilt; Weng Tonghe is dismissed from office, never to be employed again, and handed over to local officials for strict supervision.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier he was sent home, which does not answer his guilt; Weng Tonghe is dismissed forever, never to be employed again, and placed under strict supervision by local officials.

sentences.zh: 」三十年，卒於家，年七十有五。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he died at home at seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: In 1908 he died at home at seventy-five.

sentences.zh: 宣統元年，詔復原官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuantong an edict restored his former rank.
translations.idiomatic: In 1909 an edict restored his former rank.

sentences.zh: 後追諡文恭。

translations.literal: Later he was posthumously granted the title Wengong.
translations.idiomatic: He was later given the posthumous title Wengong.

sentences.zh: 同龢久侍講幃，參機務，遇事專斷。

translations.literal: Tonghe long attended the lecture seat and participated in council affairs, deciding matters on his own authority.
translations.idiomatic: Tonghe long served at the lecture seat and on the council, often deciding matters on his own.

sentences.zh: 與左右時有爭執，群責怙權。

translations.literal: He frequently quarreled with colleagues, and the group blamed him for monopolizing power.
translations.idiomatic: He quarreled often with colleagues, and many blamed him for grasping power.

sentences.zh: 晚遭讒沮，幾獲不測，遂斥逐以終。

translations.literal: In his later years he suffered slander and nearly came to harm, and was finally driven out to end his days.
translations.idiomatic: Late in life he suffered slander and nearly came to harm, and was finally expelled to end his days.

sentences.zh: 著有瓶廬詩稿八卷、文稿二十卷。

translations.literal: He authored eight fascicles of Poetic Drafts from the Bottle Studio and twenty fascicles of prose drafts.
translations.idiomatic: He left eight fascicles of Poetic Drafts from the Bottle Studio and twenty fascicles of prose.

sentences.zh: 其書法自成一家，尤為世所宗雲。

translations.literal: His calligraphy formed a school of its own and was especially revered by the world.
translations.idiomatic: His calligraphy formed a school of its own and was especially revered.

sentences.zh: 孫毓汶，字萊山，山東濟寧州人，尚書瑞珍子。

translations.literal: Sun Yuwen, style name Laishan, was a native of Jining Prefecture in Shandong and son of Minister Sun Ruizhen.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yuwen, style Laishan, was from Jining Prefecture in Shandong, son of Minister Sun Ruizhen.

sentences.zh: 咸豐六年，以一甲二名進士授編修。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Xianfeng he placed second in the jinshi examination with top honors and was appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: In 1856 he placed second in the jinshi examination and was appointed reviser.

sentences.zh: 八年，丁父憂。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he entered mourning for his father.
translations.idiomatic: In 1858 he entered mourning for his father.

sentences.zh: 十年，以在籍辦團抗捐被劾，革職遣戍。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, while at home organizing militia to resist levies, he was impeached, dismissed from office, and banished.
translations.idiomatic: In 1860, while at home organizing militia to resist tax levies, he was impeached, dismissed, and banished.

sentences.zh: 恭親王以毓汶世受國恩，首抗捐餉，深惡之。

translations.literal: Prince Gong, holding that Yuwen's family had long received imperial grace yet he was foremost in resisting levies, deeply detested him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Gong, noting that Yuwen's family had long enjoyed imperial favor yet he led resistance to levies, deeply detested him.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，以輸餉復原官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he was restored to office for contributing funds.
translations.idiomatic: In 1862 he was restored to office for contributing funds.

sentences.zh: 五年，大考一等一名，擢侍講學士。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, in the triennial examination he ranked first in the top class and was promoted to expositor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1866 he placed first in the triennial examination and was promoted to expositor.

sentences.zh: 先後典四川鄉試，督福建學政。

translations.literal: He successively presided over the Sichuan provincial examination and served as educational commissioner of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: He supervised the Sichuan provincial examination and served as educational commissioner of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 光緒元年，丁母憂。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangxu he entered mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: In 1875 he entered mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 服闋，起故官。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he resumed his former post.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he resumed his former post.

sentences.zh: 尋遷詹事，視學安徽。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was transferred to Junior Mentor and conducted an inspection tour of Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Junior Mentor and conducted an educational inspection of Anhui.

sentences.zh: 擢內閣學士，授工部左侍郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Grand Secretariat Bachelor and appointed Vice Minister of the Left in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Grand Secretariat Bachelor and Left Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 十年，命赴江南等省按事。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was ordered to investigate affairs in Jiangnan and other provinces.
translations.idiomatic: In 1884 he was ordered to investigate affairs in Jiangnan and other provinces.

sentences.zh: 時法越事起，毓汶以習於醇親王，漸與聞機要。

translations.literal: At that time the Franco-Vietnamese conflict had erupted; Yuwen, being familiar with Prince Chun, gradually came to hear confidential matters.
translations.idiomatic: When the Franco-Vietnamese war began, Yuwen, being close to Prince Chun, gradually gained access to confidential affairs.

sentences.zh: 適奉硃諭盡罷軍機王大臣，毓汶還，遂命入直軍機，兼總理各國事務大臣。

translations.literal: Just then a vermilion rescript dismissed all the Grand Councilors; when Yuwen returned he was ordered onto the Grand Council and to serve concurrently as Minister of the Office for the Management of Foreign Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: A vermilion rescript then dismissed all Grand Councilors; when Yuwen returned he was ordered onto the council and into the Office for the Management of Foreign Affairs.

sentences.zh: 時當國益厭言路紛囂，出張佩綸等會辦南北洋、閩海軍務，餘亦因事先後去之，風氣為之一變。

translations.literal: Those in power had grown weary of the censorate's clamor; Zhang Peilun and others were sent to handle North and South Sea and Fujian naval affairs, and the rest were removed one after another on various pretexts—the tone of public discourse changed at a stroke.
translations.idiomatic: Those in power had grown weary of memorialists' clamor; Zhang Peilun and others were sent to handle naval affairs, and the rest were removed on various pretexts—the tone of court debate shifted at once.

sentences.zh: 十五年，擢刑部尚書，尋調兵部，加太子少保。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was promoted to Minister of Justice, soon transferred to the Ministry of War, and granted the title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In 1889 he was promoted to Minister of Justice, soon transferred to War, and made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 歷典會試、順天鄉試，賞黃馬褂、雙眼花翎、紫韁。

translations.literal: He successively served as chief examiner of the metropolitan examination and examiner of the Shuntian provincial examination, and was granted a yellow riding jacket, double-eyed peacock feathers, and a purple bridle.
translations.idiomatic: He served as metropolitan chief examiner and Shuntian examiner, and received a yellow riding jacket, double-eyed peacock feathers, and a purple bridle.

sentences.zh: 二十年，中日媾和，李鴻章遣人齎約至。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year China and Japan made peace and Li Hongzhang sent a man bearing the treaty.
translations.idiomatic: In 1894 China and Japan made peace and Li Hongzhang sent an envoy with the treaty.

sentences.zh: 廷臣章奏凡百上，皆斥和非計。

translations.literal: Memorials from court officials numbering in the hundreds all condemned peace as no strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Hundreds of memorials from court officials condemned peace as no strategy.

sentences.zh: 翁同龢、李鴻藻主緩，俄、法、德三國亦請毋遽換約。

translations.literal: Weng Tonghe and Li Hongzao favored delay; Russia, France, and Germany also asked that ratification not be rushed.
translations.idiomatic: Weng Tonghe and Li Hongzao favored delay; Russia, France, and Germany also asked that ratification wait.

sentences.zh: 毓汶素與鴻章相結納，力言戰不可恃，亟請署，上為流涕書之，和約遂成。

translations.literal: Yuwen had long been allied with Hongzhang; he strongly argued that war could not be relied upon and urgently asked the emperor to sign; the emperor wept as he wrote his approval, and the peace treaty was concluded.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen was long allied with Li Hongzhang; he argued that war could not be trusted and urgently pressed for signature; the emperor wept as he approved, and the treaty was concluded.

sentences.zh: 明年，稱疾乞休。

translations.literal: The following year he begged leave on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he asked for sick leave.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，卒，予諡文恪。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he died and was granted the posthumous title Wenge.
translations.idiomatic: In 1899 he died and received the posthumous title Wenge.

sentences.zh: 毓汶權奇饒智略，直軍機逾十年。

translations.literal: Yuwen was resourceful and possessed abundant stratagems; he served on the Grand Council for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen was resourceful and full of stratagems; he served on the Grand Council more than ten years.

sentences.zh: 初，醇親王以尊親參機密，不常入直，疏牘日送邸閱，謂之「過府」。

translations.literal: At first Prince Chun, as the emperor's father, participated in confidential affairs but did not regularly attend council sessions; memorials were sent daily to his residence for review, called "passing through the mansion."
translations.idiomatic: At first Prince Chun, as the emperor's father, took part in confidential affairs but seldom attended council; memorials went daily to his residence for review, called "passing through the mansion."

sentences.zh: 諭旨陳奏，皆毓汶為傳達。

translations.literal: Imperial instructions and memorials for the throne were all conveyed by Yuwen.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial instructions and memorials were all conveyed through Yuwen.

sentences.zh: 同列或不得預聞，故其權特重雲。

translations.literal: Colleagues sometimes could not learn of matters beforehand, and thus his power was especially great.
translations.idiomatic: Colleagues sometimes learned of affairs only afterward, so his power was especially great.

sentences.zh: 論曰：光緒初元，复逢訓政，勵精圖治，宰輔多賢，頗有振興之象。

translations.literal: The commentator says: At the beginning of Guangxu, regency was resumed and the court strove to reform; the chief ministers were largely capable men, and there was an appearance of revival.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: At the start of Guangxu, with regency resumed, the court strove to reform; chief ministers were largely capable, and revival seemed possible.

sentences.zh: 首輔文祥既逝，沈桂芬等承其遺風，以忠懇結主知，遇事能持之以正，雖無老成，尚有典型。

translations.literal: After Chief Minister Wen Xiang died, Shen Guifen and others carried on his tradition, winning the ruler's trust through loyal earnestness and upholding principle in affairs; though lacking the seasoned statesmanship of elders, they still offered a model.
translations.idiomatic: After Wen Xiang died, Shen Guifen and others carried on his style, winning trust through loyal earnestness and holding to principle; though not elder statesmen, they still set a standard.

sentences.zh: 及甲申法越、甲午日韓，外患內憂，國家多故。

translations.literal: By the jiashen Franco-Vietnamese conflict and the jiawu Sino-Japanese crisis, foreign troubles and domestic anxieties multiplied.
translations.idiomatic: By the wars of 1884 and 1894–95, foreign troubles and domestic anxieties multiplied.

sentences.zh: 慈聖倦勤，經營園囿，稍事遊幸，而政紀亦漸弛矣。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager grew weary of governing, devoted herself to gardens and pavilions, and traveled somewhat for pleasure, while political discipline gradually slackened.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager grew weary of daily rule, tended gardens and travel, and political discipline gradually slackened.

sentences.zh: 鴻藻久參樞密，眷遇獨隆。

translations.literal: Hongzao had long served on the Grand Council and enjoyed favor beyond others.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzao had long served on the Grand Council and enjoyed favor beyond his peers.

sentences.zh: 桂芬以持重見賞，同龢以專斷致嫌。

translations.literal: Guifen was valued for his steadiness; Tonghe incurred dislike for his arbitrary decisions.
translations.idiomatic: Guifen was prized for steadiness; Tonghe drew dislike for deciding matters on his own.

sentences.zh: 毓汶奔走其間，勤勞亦著，大體彌縫，賴以無事。

translations.literal: Yuwen moved busily between them; his diligence was also evident, and in broad matters he patched things together so that affairs passed without incident.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen shuttled between them, his industry evident; on broad matters he patched things together so affairs passed without crisis.

sentences.zh: 然以政見異同，門戶之爭，牽及朝局，至數十年而未已。

translations.literal: Yet because policy disagreements fed factional strife that touched the court itself, the struggle continued for decades without end.
translations.idiomatic: Yet policy disagreements fed factional strife that touched the court itself, and the struggle ran on for decades.

sentences.zh: 賢者之責，亦不能免焉。

translations.literal: Even the responsibility of worthy men could not escape it.
translations.idiomatic: Even men of talent could not escape bearing part of the blame.
